briefs.b0:
**Purpose** – These are the complete, self‑contained criteria used on 1 March 2026 to decide whether a manuscript submitted to Meridian Review will be processed (HANDLED), sent back for revision (RETURNED), or accepted after automatic figure padding (PADDED). No other information is needed.

---

### Rules

**R1 – Length**  
The manuscript must contain **≥ 22 pages**. Exactly 22 pages counts as meeting the rule.

**R2 – Format**  
Either the official template is used **or** the submission includes a documented revision history covering **at least three years**.

**R3 – Venue overlap**  
If the work was presented at any Tier‑1 venue, that presentation must have occurred **more than 18 months before the deadline**. An exact 18‑month gap does *not* satisfy R3.

**R4 – Prior rounds**  
A manuscript previously accepted in a Meridian round is disqualified unless **≥ 5 years** have passed since that acceptance. Exactly five years is acceptable.

**R5 – Paired submissions**  
A pair may contain **exactly two manuscripts**; three or more are invalid. Both items must meet R1 and R2. At least one of the two must also satisfy R3 (the other need not).

**R6 – Track D exemption**  
Submissions to Track D ignore R2, but they must instead provide **exactly two endorsements** (one is insufficient). R6 does *not* waive any other rule.

**R7 – Retraction**  
Any manuscript with an open retraction notice is automatically RETURNED, overriding every other rule (including R9).

**R8 – Figures**  
Figure count must be **between 8 and 45 inclusive**. For a paired submission the upper bound expands to **70**, while the lower bound remains 8.

**R9 – Figure adjustment**  
If a manuscript fails R8 *only* by having fewer than the minimum, it is accepted as **PADDED** (figures are added up to the minimum). Exceeding the maximum triggers RETURNED.

**R10 – Withdrawals**  
A prior‑round withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for R4. It also resets the R3 clock: the “presentation date” is treated as the withdrawal date.

---

### Verdicts

- **HANDLED** – all applicable rules satisfied.  
- **RETURNED** – any applicable rule fails (except the sole‑case padding of R9).  
- **PADDED** – only the low‑figure case of R9; if any other rule also fails, the verdict is RETURNED.

The Meridian Review (2026 round) decides whether a manuscript will be **HANDLED**, **RETURNED**, or **PADDED** based on ten independent rules evaluated as of 1 March 2026.  

**R1 – Length:** The paper must contain at least 22 pages; exactly 22 meets the rule.  

**R2 – Format:** Either use the official template *or* provide documented revision history covering three or more years. One of these suffices.  

**R3 – Venue overlap:** If the work was presented at a Tier‑1 venue, it is only eligible when that presentation occurred **more than** 18 months before the deadline. An exact 18‑month gap does not count.  

**R4 – Prior rounds:** Acceptance in an earlier Meridian round blocks handling unless at least five years have passed since that acceptance; exactly five years is acceptable.  

**R5 – Paired submissions:** Up to two papers may be submitted as a pair. Both must meet R1 and R2; at least one of the two must also satisfy R3. Three‑paper “pairs” are invalid.  

**R6 – Track D exemption:** Papers for Track D skip R2 but must instead carry **exactly two** endorsements (one is insufficient). No other rule is waived.  

**R7 – Retraction:** Any paper with an open retraction notice is automatically RETURNED, overriding all other rules, including R9.  

**R8 – Figures:** The figure count must lie between 8 and 45 inclusive; for paired submissions the upper bound rises to 70, while the lower bound remains 8.  

**R9 – Figure adjustment:** If a submission falls short of the minimum figure count, it is **PADDED** up to eight figures rather than returned. Exceeding the maximum results in RETURNED.

The Meridian Review system decides a submission’s fate on 1 Mar 2026.  
Only one verdict is issued:

* **HANDLED** – every applicable rule is satisfied.  
* **RETURNED** – at least one applicable rule fails (the exception in R9 does not apply).  
* **PADDED** – the manuscript would be HANDLED but has too few figures; it is accepted after padding to the minimum. A PADDED case that also breaks another rule becomes RETURNED.

The decision follows ten rules, evaluated in order:

1. **Length (R1)** – The text must occupy ≥ 22 pages. Exactly 22 counts as sufficient.  
2. **Format (R2)** – Either use the official template *or* provide documented revision history covering at least three years.  
3. **Venue overlap (R3)** – If the work was presented at a Tier‑1 venue, the presentation must have occurred > 18 months before the deadline; exactly 18 months is insufficient.  
4. **Prior rounds (R4)** – An earlier Meridian acceptance blocks handling unless ≥ 5 years have passed since that round. Withdrawals do not count as acceptances.  
5. **Paired submissions (R5)** – Exactly two manuscripts may be linked; each must meet R1 and R2, and at least one of the pair must satisfy R3.  
6. **Track D exemption (R6)** – Submissions to Track D ignore R2 but must carry exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is not enough. No other rule is waived.  
7. **Retraction (R7)** – Any open retraction notice forces RETURNED, overriding every other rule, including R9.  
8. **Figures count (R8)** – Must contain 8–45 figures inclusive; a paired submission may have up to 70 figures but still needs at least 8.  
9. **Figure adjustment (R9)** – If a manuscript falls short of the minimum figure count, it is PADDED up to eight and treated as HANDLED; exceeding the maximum causes RETURNED.  
10. **Withdrawals effect (R10)** – A prior‑round withdrawal resets the R3 clock: the presentation date is considered the withdrawal date for the 18‑month test.

Apply these rules exactly as written; the first rule that fails determines a RETURNED verdict, except when R9 supplies the PADDED outcome.

**Purpose** – This guide tells you how the 2026 Meridian Review decides whether a submission is **HANDLED**, **RETURNED**, or **PADDED**. Apply every rule as it stood on 1 March 2026; the first rule that disqualifies a paper determines the verdict, except where PADDED overrides a single figure‑count shortfall.

**R1 – Length** The manuscript must contain *at least* 22 pages. Exactly 22 pages counts as meeting R1.

**R2 – Format** Either (a) use the official template **or** (b) attach documented revision history covering ≥ 3 years. Satisfying one side is sufficient.

**R3 – Venue overlap** If the work was presented at a Tier‑1 venue, the presentation must have occurred *more than* 18 months before the deadline. Exactly 18 months does **not** satisfy R3.

**R4 – Prior rounds** An earlier acceptance counts as an “old” submission only if ≥ 5 years have passed since that round. Fewer than five years fails R4.

**R5 – Paired submissions** You may submit exactly two linked manuscripts; three or more is forbidden. Each must meet R1 and R2 independently, and **at least one** of the pair must also satisfy R3 (the other need not).

**R6 – Track D exemption** Manuscripts for Track D are exempt from R2 but must carry *exactly* two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient. No other rule is waived.

**R7 – Retraction override** Any paper with an open retraction notice is automatically **RETURNED**, regardless of every other rule (including R9).

**R8 – Figures** Figure count must be between 8 and 45 inclusive. For a paired submission the upper bound rises to 70, but the minimum remains 8.

You are holding a set of submission-handling rules. A colleague who has never seen those rules, and never will, has to decide real cases with them. The note you are about to write is the only thing they will have: they cannot ask you anything afterwards, they cannot look at the source, and the verdicts they issue are final.

Write the note. Cover what the scheme is for and what each rule requires, so your colleague can decide cases they have not seen. Write between 180 and 260 words. Output the note and nothing else: no preamble, no sign-off.
